confusions.moment: Running phase: three loading lines (이해관계자가 문서를 읽고 있습니다... etc.) advance on a fixed 2.5s timer.

confusions.evidence: LoadingSteps.tsx:14-19 advances currentStep purely on a setInterval(2500ms), capped at steps.length-1 — it is NOT tied to actual LLM progress. confusions.concrete_fix: Add a reassurance line that the last step keeps showing while waiting (e.g. '거의 다 됐습니다 — 잠시만요'), and ideally show an elapsed/estimate or a subtle indeterminate bar so the frozen final step doesn't read as a hang.

confusions.moment: Results phase opens with a reward summary of pills: 핵심 리스크 N건 / 침묵의 리스크 N건 / 승인 조건 N건.

confusions.evidence: FeedbackResult.tsx:164-166 and :279-281 render result.overall_reaction inside curly quotes (“...”) attributed to the persona's name/avatar, with zero 'AI 예측' / 'simulated' marker anywhere. A first-timer can read these as verbatim real quotes from a named person.

confusions.evidence:
FeedbackResult.tsx:300-311 — concerns render as static

in bordered divs with no checkbox, no 'mark as addressed', no 'send to refine' affordance. confusions.moment: Persona detail shows an accuracy-rating card: '이 피드백의 정확도를 평가해주세요' with 1-5 stars and 질문 예측/칭찬 포인트/우려·지적/추가 요구 chips.
confusions.user_thought: 정확도? 내가 이걸 어떻게 알아? 이 사람은 가상 인물인데 뭐가 정확한지 내가 어떻게 판단하지? 안 하면 안 되나?
confusions.evidence: FeedbackResult.tsx:412-453 — asks a first-time user to rate the 'accuracy' of feedback from a SAMPLE/fictional persona they never met, against a document they may have just pasted. There is no explanation of why rating matters (it feeds learning) and no way to tell it's optional. The chips (질문 예측 etc.) are unlabeled jargon for a first-timer.
confusions.concrete_fix: Reframe the prompt to be answerable and clearly optional: '이 반응이 실제 OOO의 반응과 비슷한가요? (건너뛰어도 됩니다)' / 'Does this match how this person would really react? (optional).' Add a one-liner on why: '평가하면 다음 리허설이 더 정확해집니다.' Make the chips self-explanatory ('예상 질문이 맞았나요?').

confusions.moment: Single-persona rehearsal: no synthesis, no discussion, just one card. User finishes reading it.

confusions.moment: Results overview: the only obvious forward action is the NextStepGuide card 'Next step → Refine' which renders only when project_id exists.

confusions.evidence: RehearseStep.tsx:680-686 — NextStepGuide only renders if latestFeedback?.project_id is truthy. A standalone rehearsal (manual paste, no project) gets NO next-step guidance at all after results. And the guide's reason text doesn't promise the concerns carry forward.

confusions.moment: Discussion card on multi-persona results: '토론 시작' generates a simulated meeting.

confusions.evidence: FeedbackResult.tsx:226-255 — the description text exists (good), but on click it sets discussionLoading with only a small spinner inside the button (:249) and no LoadingSteps-style staged feedback for a 2500-token call (handleStartDiscussion at RehearseStep.tsx:343-408 uses maxTokens 2500). confusions.moment: During the Q&A refine loop (round 2+), a bar labeled '명확도 / Clarity' appears with a percentage. The user is told nowhere that this number IS the convergence signal, what it measures, or that it's their 'am I done?' gauge.

The concept the whole engine calls 'convergence/수렴' (progressive-convergence.ts) is relabeled 'Clarity' with no tooltip or explanation. No legend, no 'what is this' affordance anywhere near it.

confusions.moment: The engine computes is_converged, estimated_rounds_left (e.g. '1 round left'), and trend ('improving/stable/declining') for every round, but the UI shows none of them — only score% + a generic guidance sentence.
confusions.user_thought: 내가 수렴하고 있는 건가, 아니면 제자리걸음인가? 몇 번 더 답해야 끝나지?
confusions.evidence: ConvergenceMetrics has trend, is_converged, estimated_rounds_left (types.ts:1229-1231) and they are fully computed in progressive-convergence.ts:94-110, but ConvergenceStatus (ProgressiveFlow.tsx:837-852) only renders metrics.score and metrics.guidance. Grep confirms estimated_rounds_left / is_converged / metrics.trend appear in ZERO .tsx files.
confusions.concrete_fix: In ConvergenceStatus, render the already-computed fields: a trend arrow next to the % (↑ '좋아지고 있어요' / → '안정적' / ↓ '계속 바뀌는 중') and a rounds-left chip when not converged: estimated_rounds_left>0 ? `약 ${n}번 더 답하면 완성` : '준비 완료'. Zero new computation — the data already exists on the metrics object.

confusions.moment: After answering a question, a new question appears. The convergence bar may have moved, but it sits far below the question, and the user has no clear before→after of the number itself.
confusions.user_thought: 방금 내가 답한 게 먹혔나? 이 숫자가 올라간 거야 내려간 거야?
confusions.evidence: ConvergenceStatus only shows the current score with an animated bar from 0 (ProgressiveFlow.tsx:846-847) — it animates width from 0 every render, not from the previous score, so there is no perceptible 'it went up' moment. UpdateSummaryChip (UpdateSummaryChip.tsx) shows question/assumption deltas but never the clarity/convergence number, so the score change is invisible.
confusions.concrete_fix: Animate the bar from the previous score, not 0, and show a delta badge: '+12%' in accent green when it rose, muted '−5%' when it fell, fading after 2s. Store prevScore (the snapshot already carries convergence_score per progressive-engine.ts:481) and pass it into ConvergenceStatus to compute the delta.

confusions.moment: The convergence/Clarity bar disappears entirely the moment the user reaches the 'Ready to sail' (VoyagePrepSummary) card and during the dm_feedback/refining stage — exactly when they're deciding whether to stop refining.

VoyagePrepSummary ('이 방향으로 출항해도 될까요?', ProgressiveFlow.tsx:697) is shown when shouldMix and offers '출항' vs '한 번 더 짚어보기' with NO convergence number to inform that exact choice. The dm_feedback/refining stage (phaseIdx 3, line 134) shows DMFeedback with no convergence indicator at all.

confusions.moment: The guidance sentence is the only convergence explanation, but it is tiny (10px), right-aligned in a 160px box, and easy to miss; it also uses jargon like 'Mix로 넘어갈 수 있습니다'.

confusions.concrete_fix: Bump guidance to 11-12px text-secondary and full-width below the bar. Replace internal term: '구조가 안정됐습니다. 이제 초안 작성으로 넘어가도 좋아요.' (drop 'Mix', use the user-facing '초안' wording already used in PhaseDivider '초안 완성').

confusions.moment: When score >= 75 the engine marks is_converged=true ('done'), but the UI gives no celebratory or directive 'you're done refining' signal — the bar just turns green and the same small guidance line changes.
confusions.user_thought: 이제 그만 답해도 되는 건가? 끝났다는 신호가 어디 있지?

The only visual cue is the green color class at ProgressiveFlow.tsx:832-835. The QuestionCard keeps presenting another question with meta '${answers.length+1}번째 질문' (ProgressiveFlow.tsx:2038) regardless of convergence, so a converged user is still nudged to keep answering.
confusions.concrete_fix: When is_converged, replace/augment the next QuestionCard area with an explicit done-state banner: '✓ 충분히 또렷해졌어요 — 더 답하지 않아도 출항할 수 있어요' plus a primary '출항 준비로 이동' button, and downgrade further questions to a clearly-optional collapsed '더 다듬기 (선택)' link.

confusions.moment: Clicking '한 번 더 짚어보기 / One more check' (onMore) triggers a deepening round, but the user gets no promise of what it will do to convergence and no readout afterward of whether it helped.
confusions.user_thought: 한 번 더 하면 좋아지나? 방금 한 번 더 했는데 나아진 거 맞아?

confusions.concrete_fix: After an onMore round completes, scroll to / pulse the ConvergenceStatus and show a transient line tied to the delta: '한 번 더 짚어서 명확도가 62% → 71%로 올랐어요'. If score did NOT improve, say so honestly: '이번엔 크게 달라지지 않았어요 — 지금 출항해도 좋아요' to prevent endless looping.

confusions.moment: The convergence bar color jumps red→amber→green at 50/75 thresholds, but the thresholds are invisible — the user can't tell how far 73% is from 'green/ready'.

confusions.evidence: Color thresholds hardcoded at ProgressiveFlow.tsx:832-835 (>=75 green, >=50 amber, else red) with no marker on the track showing the 75% 'ready' line.
confusions.concrete_fix: Draw a thin tick mark + label at 75% on the bar track ('출항선' / 'ready') so the user sees the goalpost and how close they are.

confusions.evidence: i18n ko.ts:42 'ensemble.convergence':'수렴도' and ko.ts:114 'coaching.refine.iterationStatus' (mentions 수렴) are defined but unused in any .tsx (grep: matches only in lib/tests/settings). confusions.user_thought: 이 점들 뭐지? 꽉 찬 점이랑 빈 점이 뭐가 다르지? 어디가 지금 위치지?
confusions.evidence: src/components/workspace/progressive/BranchMap.tsx:92-124 encodes filled/hollow/ring/flag/dim with zero on-screen legend; VoyageChart.tsx only shows a '항로 목록' list when >1 branch (:135).

confusions.moment: First-run analysis: after pressing 시작/Start, HeroFlow enters the 'analyzing' phase and streams for 20-40s. A rotating Sparkles spinner + stage label shows, but there is NO elapsed-time counter, NO 'taking longer than usual' reassurance, and NO cancel button — even though the underlying engine accepts a cancel signal.
confusions.user_thought: 뭐가 진행 중이지? 멈춘 거 아닌가? 취소도 못 하나?
confusions.evidence: src/app/workspace/page.tsx:502-532 renders the analyzing phase with only a static 'usually 20-40s' hint (line 531) and a looping spinner (527-529); handleSubmit calls runInitialAnalysis at page.tsx:221 WITHOUT passing the signal arg the engine exposes (progressive-engine.ts:293-296 `signal?: AbortSignal`). Contrast ProgressiveFlow which DOES show elapsedLabel + isLongWait + onCancel (ProgressiveFlow.tsx:385-399, 1081-1084). The very first impression is the ONE place that lacks them.
confusions.concrete_fix: Wire an AbortController in HeroFlow.handleSubmit and pass its signal to runInitialAnalysis. Add a live mm:ss counter next to the stage label, and after 30s swap the stage line to '평소보다 오래 걸려요 — 계속 진행 중 (xx초)' / 'Taking longer than usual — still working' plus a '취소'/Cancel text button that aborts and returns to idle. Reuse the elapsedSec/isLongWait pattern already in ProgressiveFlow.tsx:1062-1084.

confusions.moment: Legacy Reframe/Rehearse running phase (LoadingSteps): the loading checklist auto-advances every 2.5s and FREEZES on the last step. For a 30-40s LLM call the user stares at a frozen 'Checking approval conditions…' with a spinner for ~25-30s.
confusions.user_thought: 뭐가 진행 중이지? 마지막 줄에서 멈춘 것 같은데, 고장 났나?
confusions.evidence: src/components/ui/LoadingSteps.tsx:14-19 advances via setInterval and clamps with Math.min(prev+1, steps.length-1), so it stops at the last step after ~7.5s and never moves again; no elapsed time, no long-wait message. Used in RehearseStep.tsx:595-600 and ReframeStep.tsx:986,1092 with 3 steps.
confusions.concrete_fix: Add an optional elapsed counter + after ~25s a reassurance line ('거의 다 됐어요 — 평소보다 조금 더 걸리고 있어요' / 'Almost there — taking a bit longer than usual') to LoadingSteps. Optionally keep the last step's spinner pulsing with a subtle 'still working' subtext so it never reads as frozen.

confusions.moment: Copy button: when clipboard write fails (insecure context / permission denied / Safari focus loss), CopyButton catches the error, console.errors it, and shows nothing — the button never flips to 'Copied!', no error appears.
confusions.user_thought: 복사 눌렀는데… 됐나? 안 됐나? 아무 일도 안 일어나네.
confusions.evidence: src/components/ui/CopyButton.tsx:21-30 — the catch block at :27-29 only `console.error('Copy failed:', err)`; the success state (setCopied(true)) is unreachable on failure, so the label stays as the default and the user gets zero signal.
confusions.concrete_fix: In the catch, set a transient error state and render the button as '복사 실패 — 다시 시도'/'Copy failed — retry' for 2s (red), so the user knows it didn't work. Optionally fall back to selecting the text for manual copy.

confusions.moment: Output download (Ithaca / OutputSelector): clicking 다운로드/Download triggers a hidden anchor click and immediately revokes the blob URL, with NO toast, NO 'Downloaded' state. On browsers that drop files silently into a Downloads folder, nothing visibly happens in-app.
confusions.user_thought: 다운로드 눌렀는데 아무 변화가 없네. 내가 한 게 먹혔나? 어디로 갔지?
confusions.evidence: src/components/ui/OutputSelector.tsx:128-137 handleDownload builds a blob, calls a.click() and URL.revokeObjectURL immediately, returning no UI acknowledgement; the Download button (173-175) has no loading/done state.
confusions.concrete_fix: After a.click(), briefly flip the button to '저장됨 ✓'/'Saved ✓' for 2s (mirror CopyButton's copied pattern) and/or show a small toast '파일을 다운로드했어요 — 다운로드 폴더를 확인하세요' / 'Downloaded — check your Downloads folder'.

confusions.moment: Sending a question to a human teammate (deploy with a 'human' worker, e.g. email/Slack) when the auth session has no access token (anonymous user or expired session): the send code returns silently, the worker is never marked 'sent' or 'error', and execution proceeds.
confusions.user_thought: 동료한테 질문이 갔나? 보냈다고 떴는데 안 떴나? 진짜 전송된 거 맞아?
confusions.evidence: src/components/workspace/progressive/ProgressiveFlow.tsx:1247-1248 — `if (!authSession?.access_token) return;` bails out of the human-send loop with no store.updateWorker and no error surfaced, while the success/failure branches at :1260-1268 DO update status. The worker silently stays in its prior state.
confusions.concrete_fix: Replace the silent `return` with a per-worker error state: store.updateWorker(hw.id, { status: 'error', error: '로그인이 필요해요 — 질문을 보내려면 로그인하세요' / 'Login required to send this question' }) so the human-worker card surfaces an actionable message + Retry instead of looking sent.

confusions.moment: Saving work that exceeds localStorage quota (long sessions): the write fails silently. The user keeps typing/answering, believing it is saved, but it is not — and on reload the work is gone.
confusions.user_thought: 내가 적은 게 저장됐겠지? (사실 안 됨, 아무 신호 없음)
confusions.evidence: src/lib/storage.ts:41-43 — setStorage swallows every write failure (including QuotaExceededError) into console.error with zero UI feedback; this is the data-loss path the master plan flags as L0 P1 'silent data loss' (MASTER-DIRECTION §L0).
confusions.concrete_fix: On catch, dispatch a global toast event ('저장 공간이 가득 찼어요 — 일부 작업이 저장되지 않을 수 있어요. 오래된 프로젝트를 정리하거나 로그인해 동기화하세요' / 'Storage is full — recent work may not be saved. Clear old projects or log in to sync') and render a persistent banner until resolved.

confusions.moment: Rehearse → 'Start discussion' (토론 시작): the 30-40s discussion generation has a button-level spinner (good), but on failure it throws a raw native browser alert() instead of the app's inline red error card used everywhere else.
confusions.user_thought: 이 회색 시스템 팝업은 뭐지? 갑자기 브라우저 경고창이… 이거 앱이 맞나?
confusions.evidence: src/components/workspace/RehearseStep.tsx:402-404 — the catch calls `alert(L('토론을 생성할 수 없었습니다. ', ...) + de.message)`. Every other error in the same file uses an inline styled card with a Retry button (e.g. RehearseStep.tsx:569-578).
confusions.concrete_fix: Replace alert() with a setDiscussionError state rendered as the same inline red AlertTriangle card + '다시 시도'/Retry button used for feedbackError at :569-578.

confusions.moment: ProgressiveFlow long async waits OTHER than the main analyze/mix (iteration 'Navigator is editing…', deepening, DM feedback, finalization): they show a spinner + label but no elapsed counter and no long-wait reassurance, so a slow 40s revision looks indistinguishable from a hang.
confusions.user_thought: 수정 중이라는데 한참 됐다… 멈춘 거 아냐?
confusions.evidence: src/components/workspace/progressive/ProgressiveFlow.tsx:2628-2633 (iteration modal) shows only 'Loader2 + 항해장이 편집 중입니다…' with no timer; the elapsedSec/isLongWait machinery at :1062-1084 is wired ONLY to the PhaseStatusBar (busy/analyzing/mixing/lead_synthesizing at :1067), not to the iteration/finalization spinners.
confusions.concrete_fix: Reuse the existing elapsedSec value: append ' (xx초)' to the 'Navigator is editing…' line and, past 30s, add '평소보다 조금 더 걸려요'/'Taking a bit longer'. Same one-line treatment for the finalize/deepen spinners.

confusions.moment: Assembling phase (HeroFlow): a 2s timer auto-promotes idle→analyzing, and the 'Team assembled. Analyzing…' line appears even before any real token has arrived. If the network is slow, the team-assembly animation plays and then the analyzing card sits empty ('Searching…' / '대기 중') with no indication the request hasn't actually reached the server yet.
confusions.user_thought: 팀이 모였다는데 화면은 텅 비어있네 — 분석이 진짜 시작된 거야, 아니면 그냥 애니메이션이야?
confusions.evidence: src/app/workspace/page.tsx:213-215 sets a 2000ms timer flipping assembling→analyzing regardless of whether runInitialAnalysis has produced a first token; the real first-token handler at :223-227 also flips it. So 'analyzing' can render with empty fields (page.tsx:545,579,611 show 'Searching…'/'대기 중') before any server response.
confusions.concrete_fix: Gate the analyzing card's 'live' fields on first-token-received; until then show a single honest line 'AI 팀에 연결하는 중…' / 'Connecting to the AI team…' so an empty analyzing card never reads as a stall.

confusions.moment: validation_failed worker — the 'Use anyway' (그냥 사용) escape hatch: a worker whose output FAILED quality validation can be accepted with one click, and the philosophy-critical engine path even auto-accepts a failed result after a timeout with no user awareness.
confusions.user_thought: 품질 확인이 필요하다는데… 그냥 써도 되나? 이거 통과 안 된 건데 내가 뭘 승인하는 거지?
confusions.evidence: src/components/workspace/progressive/WorkerCard.tsx:286-287 — '그냥 사용'/'Use anyway' flips a validation-FAILED worker straight to status:'done' with no confirmation of what failed; the master plan also flags worker-engine.ts:267-269/282-284 silently auto-accepting a FAILED result (MASTER-DIRECTION §L0 'silent auto-accept'). The user has no clear signal that they're overriding a real quality gate.
confusions.concrete_fix: Keep the button but make the override explicit: relabel to '확인했어요, 그대로 사용'/'I reviewed it — use as-is' and add a one-line caption '품질 점검을 통과하지 못한 결과예요'/'This did not pass the quality check'. Per the plan, the engine must never silently auto-accept — block on retry/timed_out, not accept.

ux.surface: mobile-end-to-end (~375px viewport): workspace HeroFlow → ProgressiveFlow voyage → Logbook/Worker drawers → FinalCard 이타카, plus modals

confusions.moment: HeroFlow idle: I type a sentence and tap the gold 시작 button — nothing visibly changes for ~2s while the team 'assembles'. On mobile the assembling card animates in BELOW the fold (page is max-w-2xl, input is mid-screen) so I may not see it.
confusions.user_thought: 내가 한 게 먹혔나? 눌렸나?
confusions.evidence: src/app/workspace/page.tsx:381 (Start button onClick handleSubmit), :205-216 (setPhase('assembling') then 2s timer to 'analyzing'); the assembling/analyzing motion.div at :469 and :502 render in the same max-w-2xl column at :300 with no scroll-into-view call after submit
confusions.concrete_fix: On handleSubmit, immediately scroll the input/echo pill into view (requestAnimationFrame → inputRef.current.scrollIntoView({block:'start'})) AND set the button to a pressed/disabled state with an inline spinner + label '팀을 부르는 중...' so the tap registers visibly before the phase swap.

confusions.moment: Voyage in progress: the sticky PhaseStatusBar is pinned at top-14 (56px), but the global Header is also sticky top-0 z-40 and the StatusBar is z-30. On a 375px screen during a long LLM wait, the '상황을 분석하고 있습니다 · 0:42 · 취소' bar can sit directly under the header with no gap.
confusions.user_thought: 뭐가 진행 중이지? 이게 멈춘 건가?
confusions.evidence: src/components/layout/Header.tsx:90 (header sticky top-0 z-40); src/components/workspace/progressive/ProgressiveFlow.tsx:1905 (status wrapper sticky top-14 z-30); PhaseStatusBar elapsedLabel/onCancel at :385-399
confusions.concrete_fix: Confirm top-14 matches the real 56px header on mobile (it does: pt-8 etc), and add a 1px shadow/divider under the sticky status wrapper (e.g. shadow-[var(--shadow-xs)]) so the two stacked sticky strips read as separate layers rather than one ambiguous band.

confusions.moment: Two fixed bottom bars at once: once workers are deployed AND waypoints exist, the Worker bar sits at bottom-0 (56px tall) and the Logbook bar sits at bottom-[56px] (52px tall), so the bottom ~108px of the viewport is two stacked gold-bordered bars. A first-timer sees two near-identical bars and doesn't know which is which.
confusions.user_thought: 이게 두 개 뭐지? 뭘 눌러야 하지?
confusions.evidence: WorkerPanel.tsx:399 (WorkerDrawer fixed bottom-0 min-h-[56px]); Logbook.tsx:311 (LogbookDrawer fixed bottom-[56px] when offset, min-h-[52px]); both rendered together at workspace/page.tsx:132-133
confusions.concrete_fix: Give the two bars clearly distinct identity: the Logbook bar already has Compass + '항해일지'; ensure the Worker bar leads with the Team avatar row + '팀' label and a different border tint, and add a hairline gap/shadow between them. Consider merging into one segmented bottom bar with two labeled tabs (항해일지 | 팀) when both are present.

confusions.moment: Bottom-bar padding math: the content column reserves pb-[calc(120px+safe-area)] when hasWorkers, but 120px assumes worker bar 56 + log bar 56 + slack. The log bar is actually 52px and only present when waypoints exist; when there are workers but NO waypoints yet, only the 56px worker bar shows yet 120px is still reserved — and conversely a tall wrapped worker bar (avatars + 팀 N/N + 입력 + 진행 chips wrapping to 2 lines via flex-wrap) can exceed 56px and overlap the last line.
confusions.user_thought: 마지막 줄이 바에 가려졌나? 다 본 게 맞나?
confusions.evidence: workspace/page.tsx:114 (pb-[calc(120px+env(safe-area-inset-bottom))] when hasWorkers, else 64px when showRail); WorkerPanel.tsx:408 'flex items-center gap-2 flex-wrap' can wrap the chips past the 56px min-height the padding assumes
confusions.concrete_fix: Stop hard-coding 120px. Either prevent the worker bar content from wrapping (flex-nowrap + truncate the avatar/chip row) so it stays a fixed 56px, or measure the stacked bar height via a ref and set the content padding-bottom from it. At minimum bump the worker-present padding so a 2-line worker bar + 52px log bar + safe-area always clears.

confusions.moment: Worker review stepper: when workers are deployed I land on a one-at-a-time card with tiny progress dots and 'N/total'. The Prev/Later text links are at the bottom and the dots are at the top-right — on a 375px screen the dots are 2-8px wide tap targets spaced 1.5 apart.
confusions.user_thought: 이거 눌러도 되나? 어디를 눌러야 다음으로 가지?
confusions.evidence: ProgressiveFlow.tsx:2083-2091 (dot buttons w-2 h-2 / active w-5 h-2, gap-1.5, each a clickable <button>) and :2116-2126 (Prev/Later as plain text links, no min-h-[44px])
confusions.concrete_fix: Make the dot strip non-interactive (display only) on mobile and rely on the Prev/Later/Advance buttons; give those buttons min-h-[44px] + a bordered pill style so they read as the obvious navigation, not faint gray text. Or wrap each dot in a 44px tappable padding box.

confusions.moment: FinalCard completion: the three follow-up actions (새 프로젝트 시작 / 항해장에게 수정 요청 / 이해관계자 검증 다시 하기) stack full-width on mobile (flex-col), all roughly equal weight. A first-timer who just got their document doesn't know which is 'I'm done, save this' vs 'redo'.
confusions.user_thought: 이제 뭘 해야 하지? 어느 걸 눌러야 안전하지?
confusions.evidence: ProgressiveFlow.tsx:2435-2447 — three buttons in 'flex flex-col sm:flex-row', gold primary + two outline; the helper copy at :2433-2434 says 'copy and use it right away' but the actual Copy control is the ShareBar up in FinalCard (FinalCard.tsx:70)
confusions.concrete_fix: On mobile, surface the primary Copy action as a full-width button at the top of this block (the real next action is 'copy my result'), demote the three management buttons below a divider labeled '또는' and shrink them to text/secondary. Keep only one gold button visible.

confusions.moment: FinalCard ShareBar lives in the card header next to '완성된 기획안 · 바로 보낼 수 있어요'. On a 375px header that flex row (icon+title+sublabel on the left, ShareBar on the right) can crowd; the most important first-run action — Copy — is a small control competing with the title.
confusions.user_thought: 복사 버튼이 어디 있지? 이거 맞나?
confusions.evidence: FinalCard.tsx:60-75 (header 'flex items-center justify-between', left block has title + '바로 보낼 수 있어요' :67, right is <ShareBar> with copyLabel '복사')
confusions.concrete_fix: On mobile stack the ShareBar onto its own full-width row under the title (the header is already justify-between; add flex-col on <sm) and make the Copy button the visually dominant element with the '복사' label always shown (not icon-only).

confusions.moment: Logbook 'Also include the decision log when copying' checkbox: a tiny native checkbox with an 11px gray label, right-aligned in a thin row. On mobile it's an easy mis-tap and the consequence (copying 2-3x the text) is invisible until you paste.
confusions.user_thought: 이거 체크하면 뭐가 달라지지? 눌러도 되나?
confusions.evidence: FinalCard.tsx:76-83 — label text-[11px] text-tertiary, native checkbox, row 'justify-end'; tooltip-free
confusions.concrete_fix: Replace with a small labeled toggle pill ('문서만 복사' / '+결정 과정') with a min 44px tap height and a one-line preview hint ('결정 과정까지 붙으면 길이가 2~3배 길어져요'), left-aligned for thumb reach.

confusions.moment: VoyageChart 'compare' view inside the Full-chart modal renders two snapshot cards in a fixed 'grid grid-cols-2'. Inside Modal's max-w-lg mx-4 (so ~343px on a 375px screen, minus p-6 padding) two columns of real-question text become unreadably narrow.
confusions.user_thought: 글씨가 왜 이렇게 잘리지? 뭘 비교하라는 거지?
confusions.evidence: VoyageChart.tsx:243 'grid grid-cols-2 gap-2' for the compare panel; Modal.tsx:108 'max-w-lg mx-4' + :122 'p-6' content padding squeezes it on mobile
confusions.concrete_fix: Make the compare grid responsive: 'grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2' so the two snapshots stack vertically on phones, and reduce Modal content padding to p-4 on <sm.

confusions.moment: VerificationGate bottom sheet: it's a soft gate with the primary 'Set sail' button DISABLED until I review everyone, and the only enabled path is a faint gray text link '확인 없이 모두 반영하고 출항' below it. On mobile a first-timer sees a big disabled gold button and a tiny gray line and feels stuck.
confusions.user_thought: 출항 버튼이 회색이네 — 어떻게 진행하라는 거지?
confusions.evidence: VerificationGate.tsx:114-122 (onSail button disabled when !allClear, shows 'N개 남음') and :125-130 (override is text-[12px] text-tertiary link)
confusions.concrete_fix: When items remain, make the override a real secondary button (bordered, min-h-[44px]) with explicit copy '검토 없이 다 반영하고 출항 (N개)' so there is always one obvious enabled action, and keep the disabled primary as the 'recommended after review' path.

confusions.moment: Worker bar tap → half-sheet (max-h-[75vh]) reuses the full AgentSidebar. There is no drag handle and the only close affordance is a top-right X; the backdrop is bg-black/30. A non-technical user may not realize they can tap outside to dismiss, and the sheet covers the whole screen.
confusions.user_thought: 이거 어떻게 닫지? 뒤로 돌아가려면?
confusions.evidence: WorkerPanel.tsx:434-456 (sheet, X close at :447, backdrop onClick at :433 but visually subtle); no grabber bar
confusions.concrete_fix: Add a visible drag-handle pill at the top of the sheet (a centered 36x4px rounded bar) and keep the X; the handle is the universal 'this is a dismissible sheet' signal on mobile.

confusions.moment: Logbook waypoint rows are tappable accordions (line-clamp-2 → expand) but the whole row click target is min-h-[20px] with a 12px chevron. The nested 'fork a new course here' / 'Sail this path' actions are 10px text links. On mobile this dense 항해일지 reads as static text, not interactive.
confusions.user_thought: 이게 눌리는 건가? 어디를 눌러야 펼쳐지지?
confusions.evidence: Logbook.tsx:195-214 (toggle button 'min-h-[20px]'), :237-243 ('이 길 가보기' text-[10px]), :266-273 ('이 시점에서 다른 길로' text-[10px])
confusions.concrete_fix: Raise the waypoint row tap target to min-h-[44px] inside the mobile sheet, and render the fork/sail actions as small bordered chips (not bare links) so their tappability is obvious to a non-dev.

confusions.moment: During 'assembling', the problem echo pill uses 'truncate' so a long pasted problem is cut to one line with an ellipsis; later in the live voyage the same echo at the top is also truncate. The user can't confirm the full text the team received.
confusions.user_thought: 내가 쓴 내용이 제대로 들어간 게 맞나?
confusions.evidence: workspace/page.tsx:478 (assembling echo 'truncate'); ProgressiveFlow.tsx:1938 (voyage echo pill 'truncate')
confusions.concrete_fix: Make the echo pill tappable to expand the full problem text (or allow 2-line clamp on first render), so the user can verify what was submitted.

confusions.moment: Returning-user 'Continue' project rows on HeroFlow: the ChevronRight affordance is opacity-0 and only appears on group-hover, which never fires on touch. On mobile the rows look like static labels with no 'tap to open' cue.
confusions.user_thought: 이게 눌러서 들어가는 건가?
confusions.evidence: workspace/page.tsx:327 — ChevronRight 'opacity-0 md:opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100' (hover-only, no touch fallback)
confusions.concrete_fix: Show the chevron at a low opacity by default on mobile (remove the opacity-0 default under md, or use 'opacity-40 md:opacity-0 md:group-hover:opacity-100') so touch users get the tap cue.

confusions.moment: The legacy 4-tab mode (reached via ?step=) has its own fixed bottom nav (lg:hidden, bottom-0 z-40) AND a QuickChatBar AND a NavigatorStrip — three stacked bottom elements with no explicit safe-area handling on the bottom nav, so on a notched phone the labels can sit under the home indicator.
confusions.user_thought: 버튼 라벨이 왜 잘리지? 이거 다 눌리는 건가?
confusions.evidence: workspace/page.tsx:846-865 (mobile bottom nav 'fixed bottom-0' with py-1.5, no env(safe-area-inset-bottom)); QuickChatBar at :840 and NavigatorStrip at :843 also render
confusions.concrete_fix: Add pb-[env(safe-area-inset-bottom)] to the legacy bottom nav at :846 and verify QuickChatBar/NavigatorStrip don't stack on top of it on mobile (hide one, or coordinate offsets like the progressive drawers do).

confusions.moment: VoyagePrepSummary '이 방향으로 출항' is the primary CTA but two secondary links ('한 번 더 짚어보기' · '답한 내용 돌아보기') sit centered below as 12px gray text. On mobile a confused first-timer who wants to NOT commit yet sees only a big gold button and faint gray words.

uxCritic.blind_spots: The catalogue is exhaustive WITHIN each surface's happy path, but it has five systematic blind spots. (1) GLOBAL CHROME: it analyzes the landing's LandingHeader and the in-flow surfaces, but never the persistent app Header.tsx that sits on top of EVERY workspace/tool screen — its 6 nav items (Workspace/Projects/Agents/Manager/Guide/Settings), three of them lock-gated, the KO/EN toggle, and the theme toggle are an untouched source of first-run 'what are all these / can I click them' confusion, and the Header coexists with the very CTAs the catalogue proposes adding, creating a double-CTA problem nobody checked. (2) DESTRUCTIVE/STATE-LOSING GLOBAL ACTIONS: the catalogue caught storage quota silent-loss and the analyzing-cancel gap, but missed that the language toggle does a hard window.location.reload() mid-voyage (useLocaleSwitch.ts:21) — for an anonymous user with no Supabase row this is a real 'where did my work go' risk, and there is zero warning. (3) ERROR-RECOVERY DEAD-ENDS: it treats inline LLM errors well but never opened the global ErrorBoundary, whose 'Try again' merely clears hasError and re-renders the SAME crashed subtree (it will usually re-crash), and the StepErrorFallback's only action is a full page reload. (4) THE MISSING ONBOARDING ITSELF: the catalogue critiques HeroFlow's empty state copy but never states the larger fact that the master-plan's planned first-run auto-demo (gated by 'argus.has_onboarded' at workspace/page.tsx:690) DOES NOT EXIST in the code — a true first-timer gets dropped straight onto a bare textarea with no guided intro at all; the demo cards are opt-in and easy to skip. (5) RE-ENTRY / SESSION-RESUME ORIENTATION: it covers the 'Continue' rows' lack of status, but not what actually happens on click — a returning user is dropped back into the middle of a 5-stage voyage (conversing/worker/final) with no 'here's where you left off' recap, and the anonymous rate-limit counter (RateLimitBadge) is gated to logged-in users only (Header.tsx:159), so an anon user burning through ANON_LIMIT free runs never sees a remaining count until they hit the hard wall. These are the 'between/around the surfaces' confusions a per-surface sweep structurally misses.

gaps.gap: L0's stream-watchdog fix is correct but the plan omits the integration contract that makes it actually clear the infinite spinner. The ProgressiveFlow handlers only reset the spinner (setStreamingText(null), setBusy(false)) inside catch/finally of an `await runDeepening(...)` etc. If a watchdog merely aborts the reader without driving callbacks.onError, the awaited callLLMStreamThenParse promise neither resolves nor rejects, the `await` never returns, and finally never runs — the spinner stays forever even after the abort. The watchdog MUST surface through callbacks.onError (which rejects the promise) AND must not be misclassified: callLLMStream already maps AbortError → onError, and the handlers special-case `DOMException name==='AbortError'` to suppress the error UI — so a watchdog that aborts via options.signal will be silently swallowed as a user-cancel and show NO error, not the intended timeout message.
gaps.evidence: ProgressiveFlow.tsx:1397 (`catch (e) { setStreamingText(null); if (!(e instanceof DOMException && e.name==='AbortError')) setError(...) }`), :1717 (same pattern); llm.ts:748-751 (AbortError → onError, returns); callLLMStreamThenParse llm.ts:786 (onError: reject)
gaps.proposed_layer: L0 — add to the stream-hang acceptance criteria
gaps.fix: The watchdog must reject with a DISTINCT non-Abort error (e.g. LLMError category 'timeout'), not a bare signal.abort(), so the handler's `!(AbortError)` guard lets it through and the user sees a real timeout message instead of a silent no-op. Add an acceptance test asserting a hung stream produces a visible error in ProgressiveFlow, not just an aborted reader.

gaps.gap: Worker-engine 30s timeout uses Promise.race against a setTimeout that is never cleared, and the no-callback branch silent-accept is only half the philosophy bug. Even with L0's fix changing the timeout resolution to 'retry'/'timed_out', the loser setTimeout(30_000) keeps a live timer per validation-failed worker until it fires; with MAX_CONCURRENT workers this leaks timers and, more importantly, if onValidationFailed REJECTS (callback throws), Promise.race rejects, the surrounding try/catch at :286 calls onError and `break`s — so a validation-failed result whose user-prompt errored is dropped entirely (no finalResult, onComplete never called at :293-295), losing the step silently.
gaps.evidence: worker-engine.ts:267-270 (Promise.race with uncleared setTimeout), :286-290 (catch → onError + break, finalResult stays null), :293-295 (onComplete only fires if finalResult truthy)
gaps.proposed_layer: L0 — fold into the silent-auto-accept fix
gaps.fix: Clear the timeout once the race settles; treat an onValidationFailed rejection as 'timed_out'/'retry' rather than letting it fall through to the generic catch that drops the worker; ensure every validation-failed worker reaches a terminal callback (onComplete with a flagged result OR an explicit onError) so a step is never silently lost.

gaps.gap: The substring(0,8)/(0,10) assumption linkers are not merely 'false links on legacy id-less data' (the plan's framing) — they are actively WRONG on fresh data today. agent-spec.ts:104 matches an assumption to a step iff the step.task literally contains the assumption's first 8 characters; this yields false POSITIVES when two assumptions share an 8-char prefix (common in Korean/templated phrasings) and false NEGATIVES whenever the assumption is paraphrased rather than copied verbatim into the task — which is the normal case since tasks and assumptions are generated by separate prompts. So the 'validates_assumption' link emitted into the CrewAI YAML / prompt-chain is unreliable provenance right now, before any legacy concern.

gaps.proposed_layer: L3a — strengthen the acceptance from 'no false link on legacy data' to 'links are deterministically correct on fresh data'
gaps.fix: After adding the stable HiddenAssumption.id at generation (L3a), the engine that builds steps should carry the source assumption id forward explicitly (e.g. step.source_assumption_id), and the linker should join on id — not substring-match generated text. Grep-verify both substring linkers are deleted AND that the replacement is an id-join, not a longer substring.

gaps.gap: loadAndMerge re-introduces soft-deleted rows (resurrection), which the plan explicitly listed as 'moot' for the merge path but is real here. Remote query filters `!r.deleted_at` (db.ts:106), so a row soft-deleted on another device is absent from `remote`. mergeByTimestamp keeps any item present in `local` but absent from `remote` (db.ts:66-67 only adds, never removes), so the locally-cached copy survives; worse, loadAndMerge:113-119 then computes localOnly = merged minus remoteIds and UPSERTS it back to Supabase — actively un-deleting the row server-side. This is the exact R6 scenario the plan downgraded to 'lower-priority P1 in L5', but the round-trip re-upsert makes it a data-integrity bug, not just a stale read.
gaps.evidence: db.ts:106 (remote filtered `!r.deleted_at`), db.ts:57-78 mergeByTimestamp (no removal branch), db.ts:113-119 (localOnly upserted back with onConflict id)
gaps.proposed_layer: L5 — upgrade the db.ts P1 from 'mergeByTimestamp is deleted_at-unaware' to 'loadAndMerge re-upserts tombstoned rows'
gaps.fix: Fetch remote rows INCLUDING deleted_at (drop the `!r.deleted_at` prefilter or fetch a tombstone set), pass tombstones into mergeByTimestamp so a remote deleted_at newer than local wins and removes the row, and exclude tombstoned ids from the localOnly re-upsert so a deletion is never resurrected by the sync round-trip.
